title: Olive Kitteridge
author: Elizabeth Strout
summary: Thirteen linked stories set in a small Maine town, each touching in some way on a blunt, difficult retired maths teacher. Over time we see her as neighbour, mother and wife, and she becomes more than a sharp tongue.
readIf: you like precise, compassionate short fiction about ordinary people and what they hide.
skipIf: you want a single plot; it works as a novel in stories, with many shifting perspectives.

pairings.reason: Another prickly older person whose gruffness hides a lot of feeling, though in a funnier and more consoling book.
Another subtle exploration of unhappy lives that rewards slow, attentive reading.
Another study of a person looking back at how pride and restraint cost them something important.
